Package com.stzteam.features.robotlocalization.vision.sim

Class LimelightSimConfig

java.lang.Object
com.stzteam.features.robotlocalization.vision.sim.LimelightSimConfig
public class LimelightSimConfig extends Object
Configuration for a SimulatedLimelight: everything a prototype would hardcode (NT table name, camera optics, which keys to publish) lives here.

The setters are fluent and return this, so they chain: 


 var config = LimelightSimConfig.limelight3G()
         .withTableName("limelight-front")
         .withMegaTag2(true);

The camera presets start from Limelight's published specifications and are reasonable approximations, not real calibrations. If you have your camera's calibration, pass it with withCameraProperties(SimCameraProperties).

    • withTargetSpacePoses

      public LimelightSimConfig withTargetSpacePoses(boolean enabled)
      Controls publication of targetpose_cameraspace, targetpose_robotspace, camerapose_targetspace and botpose_targetspace.

      Off by default on purpose: Limelight's target-space axis convention (X right, Y down, Z outward) is the part of the schema easiest to misread, and these keys staying obviously empty is preferable to them publishing plausible but wrong numbers. If you switch them on, validate the signs against your real hardware before trusting them.

      Parameters:
      enabled - true to publish them.
      Returns:
      this same configuration.

    • withMaxSightRange

      public LimelightSimConfig withMaxSightRange(double meters)
      Distance beyond which the simulated camera stops seeing a tag.

      This is not fine tuning, it is what separates a camera from an X-ray. Photonlib does not limit the range by default, and VisionSystemSim does not model occlusion: without a limit, the camera sees every tag inside its FOV however far away it is, straight through the field walls.

      Measured against the 2026 field with the robot at (2.7, 2.6): with no limit, seven tags came in, five of them between 8 and 13 m with ambiguities from 0.6 to 0.99, and the multi-tag PnP mixed them with the two good nearby ones and returned a pose twelve metres from the robot and a metre and a half off the ground.

      The 7 m default is what a Limelight 3G reliably resolves on a 16.5 cm tag. If you measure yours, use the number you measured.

      Parameters:
      meters - maximum range in metres.
      Returns:
      this same configuration.

    • withMinTargetAreaPixels

      public LimelightSimConfig withMinTargetAreaPixels(double pixels)
      Minimum area in pixels for a tag to count as detected.

      It is the other brake against impossible tags: one far away covers a handful of pixels and no real detector picks it out. Photonlib uses 100 by default; here it is 200, which at 1280x800 corresponds roughly to the useful limit of a 16.5 cm tag.

      Parameters:
      pixels - minimum area in pixels.
      Returns:
      this same configuration.

    • withBotposeVariants

      public LimelightSimConfig withBotposeVariants(LimelightSimConfig.BotposeVariant... variants)
      Chooses which origins the robot pose is published in.

      All three are published by default, which is what a real Limelight does. If your robot code only reads one --- the normal case --- keeping just that one cuts two thirds of the NetworkTables bandwidth this camera spends. 

      config.withBotposeVariants(BotposeVariant.WPI_BLUE);
      Parameters:
      variants - the origins to publish; with no arguments, none are published.
      Returns:
      this same configuration.

    • withRawStream

      public LimelightSimConfig withRawStream(boolean enabled)
      Publishes, over CameraServer, the raw MJPEG stream photonlib renders: the AprilTags as seen from the camera, at <name>-raw. It shows up in Glass, Shuffleboard or AdvantageScope.

      Off by default because it renders with OpenCV on every frame and costs real CPU.

      Parameters:
      enabled - true to publish it.
      Returns:
      this same configuration.
